claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a fine fcc/B2 dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The lamellae alternate between soft fcc and hard B2 phases.
Stress concentration at the continuous phase interfaces causes catastrophic cracking in the as-cast alloy.
The as-cast alloy has a strain-hardening ratio σ_UTS/σ_0.2 close to 16.
The high strain-hardening ratio originates from dislocation storage in the fine lamellar structure containing alternating soft fcc and hard B2 phases.
Room-temperature severe plastic deformation will introduce a high defect density and break the continuity of the lamellae.
Annealing at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for four hours after SPD will rearrange and coarsen the phases into a patterned configuration without melting.
A temperature of 1230 °C is within the eutectic stability range of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and below its melting temperature.
A pressure of 152 MPa is sufficient to suppress void nucleation and promote phase stability in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Dislocation-mediated phase-boundary migration will fragment the continuous lamellae.
The resulting patterned structure will consist of discrete, rounded B2-rich islands in a continuous fcc matrix.
Continuous interfaces in the initial lamellar structure act as crack-propagation paths.
Breaking continuous lamellae into isolated islands lowers interfacial energy.
Applying 152 MPa during annealing prevents microvoid formation and suppresses brittle fracture.
A continuous reticulated Laves-phase distribution in another high-entropy alloy hindered crack propagation and increased fracture strain.
The island-in-matrix structure will reduce catastrophic interfacial cracking and increase room-temperature uniform elongation.
The treated alloy will maintain or slightly improve yield strength because it retains a fine dispersion of hard phases.
Pressure above 6 GPa can cause an unwanted fcc-to-hcp transformation.
The eutectic reaction in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is isothermal.
HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for four hours caused secondary HCP-phase precipitation and tensile brittleness in Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that 152 MPa suppresses brittle fracture, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that the cited HIP treatment at the same pressure and temperature produced extreme tensile brittleness in the transferred alloy system.

The baseline field defines the as-cast alloy as the baseline, but the experiment and falsification rule call the HIP-only sample the baseline; no untreated as-cast group is included in the stated two-group experiment.
